_comment: Running list of player-facing patch notes for the NEXT release. As work ships, append entries here. The patch-notes skill rolls this into Assets/data/patchnotes.json on release and clears pending. Categories: feature, balance, fix, polish, content.

entries.line: Open Beta launched — welcome popup added on first menu open of each session
Roadmap reframed around the road to v1.0 full release: Tower Mode, Guilds Return, and Ranked Battling now headlining the in-development column
Starter selection screen no longer renders a giant yellow rectangle when picking a beast
Selected starter now reads more clearly via a bigger element-tinted glow with a warm bronze rim
Guild UI hidden during open beta to focus playtest feedback on core systems (data preserved — UI returns post-beta)

Leaderboards reset for the open beta — pre-launch playtest data was inflating every category. Raid runs no longer count as battle wins, aggregation is now explicit (Max), and a one-time migration zeroes both local counters and public boards on first launch.
Achievements panel no longer opens to a black screen — modal frame was collapsing to zero height
Swapping a beast mid-turn no longer lets the enemy hit the OUTGOING beast off-screen — attacks now retarget to the new active. Thanks Veauph for the report!
Skill tree clusters got a Persona-style stamp pass — colored gradient cluster headers with corner cuts, halftone wash, hard offset shadows on stat pills
Close (X) buttons unified across every panel — same size, same hover spin, same red-tint dismissal feedback. No more 8 different X buttons depending on which screen you're on.
Confirm dialogs unified — destructive action (Leave/Disband/Kick/etc.) is always on the LEFT, Cancel always on the RIGHT. Same chrome and button order across Arena, Guild, and end-expedition prompts.
Empty states (no beasts found, no inventory item selected, leaderboard empty, shop filter empty) now share the same diamond-frame icon + title + body design.
Help panel sidebar redesigned to match Quest panel — taller tabs, real iconify icons (no more emoji squares), short descriptive subtitles, left-accent strip on the active tab.
Credits panel header now matches the Achievement / Feedback / Options modal-popup chrome instead of being its own one-off.
Section titles inside panels are now consistently 11px with a purple left accent bar.
Starter mid- and final-evo wilds now drop named themed materials — Vigil Ember, Sentinel Bristle, Mourning Scale, Abyss Tooth, Warden Plume, Halo Shard. No more 'Pyrgard Spirit' placeholders.
Roadmap popup got the Persona stamp pass — diagonal-gradient section heads with halftone wash, italic-skew version tags with hard offset shadows, sharp-edged column tabs keyed by section color

Help / Game Guide redesigned — Persona-stamp sidebar tabs with nested subtab navigation, modal-popup chrome matching Options/Achievements, screenshot slots, and a P5 visual vocabulary throughout. Beasts and Fusion sections rewritten from current code (gene scale 0–30, soft cap 25+, Quality tiers from real total-of-180 math, 17 natures, 7 Veteran Ranks).
Help content uses 'contract' instead of 'catch' across the board, and dropped stale references to the removed loyalty system.

Chat profanity filter — slurs and crude language are auto-replaced with asterisks across global, trade, and guild channels. Filtering happens on both send and receive so modded clients can't push raw text to other players.

Skill Tree → Stats subtab — see every player-wide modifier (gold, XP, contract rate, drop rates, fusion bonuses, all-beast ATK/HP, boss damage, healing) with each contributing source (skill rank, equipped relic, active boost, guild perk, double-XP event, Elite Ink) broken out so you can see exactly where every percentage is coming from. Sample-expedition gold worked example at the top makes the math concrete.

Interactive tutorial — new players are walked through their first expedition and first contract on a tutorial-only zone (Saltmoor Approach). Two-mode hint UI: centered speech bubble for info beats, non-blocking top banner for action beats that lets you actually click the thing it's pointing at. First contract is rigged to succeed so the win lands. Player keeps every reward including the contracted Beast, plus a +50 Contract Ink completion bonus. Skip with a confirmation; replay any time from Options.
Tutorial 'weaken the wild Beast' step now actually advances when the enemy drops below half HP — manual battles were bypassing the damage hook.
Tutorial 'open negotiations' step now advances when you click the Contract button mid-battle — the hook was only wired to the legacy Tame Workshop entry point.
Tutorial contract step is now bulletproof: the rigged confirm bypasses ink/gold checks and the player gets topped up to 5 Contract Ink on entry, so a replayed tutorial can never brick on resources.

Tutorial action steps now actually show the spotlight + a giant pulsing arrow pointing at the thing you should click — was previously broken because the selector and root-panel walk were both wrong. Arrow auto-orients (above/below/left/right) based on where the target sits on screen.

Reset Game Data is now locked while the tutorial is in progress — previously you could wipe your save mid-tutorial and end up in a broken intermediate state with no Saltmoor Approach zone to return to.
Open Beta welcome popup got the Persona-stamp slab pass — sharp 4px corners, hard offset gold shadow, skewed 'Alert · Beta' corner tag, dotted halftone wash.

Now Hiring — main menu has a new pulsing pill above the Discord link that opens a recruitment popup. We're looking for developers (C# / s&box / UI / backend), pixel artists (sprites / animations / FX), and 3D pixel modelers (environment tiles / props / zone dressing). Apply in the Beastborne Discord.

Main menu got the Persona-stamp pass — top-left LIVE ticker is now a skewed yellow stamp pill, bottom-right NEW badge is a skewed yellow stamp, the WHAT'S NEW tooltip became a P5 slab with hard offset gold shadow, and the active-event toast got the same stamp chrome with a hard offset purple shadow.

Patch Notes panel restamped — sharp 4px corners, 2px black border, hard offset purple shadow, skewed 'WHAT'S NEW' corner tag, version pill is now a skewed purple stamp, section heads became colored stamp pills (purple Features / blue Polish / green Fixes / orange Balance), bullets are now category-tinted diamond chips, footer Discord link is a P5 slab.

Wild drop pool slimmed for launch — medicines (Berserk Tonic / Iron Skin Oil / Quickstep Powder / Arcane Draught / Warding Salve / Hunter's Focus), training treats (Training Treat / Training Feast), and contract incenses no longer drop in the wild. They moved to the shop's Supplies tab as buyable consumables. Wild zones now drop signature beast materials (the species' named loot) plus a small set of held items / relics. Way more readable drop list per zone.

World map redesigned — temporary 'Serpinglin' illustrated map by guest artist replaces the gradient placeholder. Seven hoverable village landmarks (Embrik's Watch, The Old Roost, The Almonry, Sundial House, The Holding Pens, The Quiet Pit, The Long Bridge) each show a lore tooltip on hover. Three expedition zones renamed to fit the new region: Serpinglin Outskirts (Lv 1), The Witherwood (Lv 15), Mirrorpond (Lv 30). Existing zone IDs unchanged — battles, results, leaderboards keep working.

Expedition map chrome got the Persona-stamp pass — zone markers became diamond stamp pins (sharp 4px corners, hard offset shadow), zone labels became P5 slabs, the zone-detail pane and trade popup are now stamp slabs with hard offset purple/gold shadows, EMBARK button is a red stamp slab with hard offset purple shadow, hover preview cards match.

Beast level cap lowered from 100 to 50 to match the Tamer cap — every level matters more, and the XP curve hits its meaty mid-game tier right at the ceiling. Existing beasts above 50 are clamped to 50 on load with stats recomputed; nothing else carries over differently.

Profile card got the Persona-stamp pass — sharp 4px corners, 2px black borders, hard offset shadows keyed to your arena rank (Mythic = pink, Legendary = gold, etc), skewed 'TAMER · LV N' corner tag, level number now an italic-skew stamp, avatar reframed as a slab with a sealed rank badge, ARENA / CAREER STATS / FAVORITES / PROGRESSION sections each get a colored stamp section head, every stat card and progression pill is now a tinted stamp slab with a diamond chip bullet.

Profile titles fixed — the level-tier list referenced Master Tamer at Lv 60 and Legendary Tamer at Lv 80 from before the cap was lowered. Now: Lv 1 Tamer / 10 Apprentice / 20 Skilled / 30 Expert / 40 Master / 50 Legendary, so 'Legendary Tamer' is actually reachable at the cap.

Profile card follow-up rev — Favorite Expedition and Tamer Cards sections cut (the cards button was redundant with the achievements progression pill, which is now itself clickable). Emoji currency icons replaced with iconify lucide icons (coins / gem / feather / trophy). Layout broken out of the all-horizontal cadence: arena now sits beside a vertical resources sidebar, career stats are an asymmetric featured-stat-plus-grid, favorites and the beast collection slab live side-by-side, and progression became labeled gradient meter bars (lifted from the Beastiary stat-bar pattern) with the achievements meter doubling as the Achievements button.

Profile card slimmed down — dropped the resource sidebar (already in HUD), the career stats grid (six low-signal counters), and the skills/expeditions/trades footer mini-row. Card now reads in one glance: identity, arena rank, favorite beast, beastiary discovery, achievements.

Profile card pulled back from the constant skewed-stamp tic — now exactly one iconic angled tag (the rank corner stamp 'TAMER · LV N'), and everything else reads as clean upright rectangles. Same Persona vocabulary (sharp corners, 2px black borders, hard offset shadows, halftone, diamond bullets, hard text-shadows), less visual whiplash. Also fixed the '1/146Discovered' spacing bug on the discovery slab.

Guild plaza now shows Announcement and Description as a paired two-card row instead of one super-long strip. Both editable inline by officers — pencil chip in the header, save right there, no drawer dive.

Guild Settings is now a side drawer that slides in from the right instead of a center popup — keeps the plaza visible behind it, dismisses on backdrop click, and lays out emblem and membership rules as labeled stamp slabs.

Guild Weekly Goals — three community missions every week (Wild Hunt / Contract Drive / Treasury Push and friends) that aggregate progress across every guild member. Big chunks of guild XP per goal (5,000–7,500 each) push the guild level. Lives in the Quests panel under a new Guild tab; resets Monday at 00:00 UTC.

Guild reset for v1.0.2 — every guild was wiped to clear pre-launch playtest data. Re-found or rejoin a guild fresh; level curve is now the multi-year design (Lv 50 = 3.75M XP) and weekly goals are part of how you climb it.

Profile card eased back from the heavy stamp treatment — kept the iconic rank-color outer shell, corner tag, and giant level number, but softened internal slabs (thinner borders, gentler drop shadows, calm 8px corners, bare LEVEL eyebrow instead of the bright yellow pill, achievements row no longer flooded gold), so the card reads as one strong visual instead of eight competing stamps. Rank icons swapped from Unicode glyphs to lucide iconify icons (crown for Legendary, trophy for Master, gem for Diamond, sparkles for Mythic, etc.).

Found-a-Guild flow restamped to match the rest of the panel — Persona slab header with skewed yellow corner tag, Identity and Emblem as labeled stamp cards, live preview card on the right with shape-aware emblem and tag/level stamps, gold cost row, big red FOUND GUILD slab CTA. Replaces the old generic header + flat input form.

Brand-new guilds no longer show a -109% XP bar at Lv 1 — the cumulative-XP threshold for the starting level was being read as 230, so a 0-XP guild displayed (0 − 230) / 210. Lv 1 now correctly returns 0 and the bar starts at 0 / 440 to next.
